v32_text: Sources: docs/dem_governing_equations_report_20261009.md §1 (literature form ↔ implemented form ↔ source lines of LIGGGHTS-PUBLIC 3.8.0, commit 3d5c00f) and §3 (deck values); docs/dem_governing_equations_background_20261011.md §2.3 (order of one time step: contact detection → contact forces → integration → update), §3.1 (translational and rotational equations, eqs 1–2), §5.2 (k1 from E*, R*, m* and V), §5.3 (hooke/hysteresis), §6 (tangential spring with Coulomb limit), §7 (rolling resistance, CDT), §8.2 (global viscous damping), §9 (compression procedure), §11 (limits). Equations ①–⑤, the force diagram and the process strip are copied from the author's 10-09 slide: equation objects and pictures unchanged, Korean labels translated, project header removed. Qualifiers: these are the implemented equations of the LIGGGHTS-PUBLIC 3.8.0 hooke/hysteresis model [2], read from the source code, not re-derived by a run; the linear hysteretic law (loading stiffness k1, unloading/reloading stiffness k2, adhesion branch −k_c δ) follows Luding 2008 [1]; ③ shows the non-saturated branch only (the saturated branch and the k2(δmax) interpolation are in the report); ④ shows the spring part (tangential damping in non-slip steps is omitted); k_t = k_n in this model; the rolling torque uses k_n δ, not the hysteretic normal force; k1 depends on mass and the characteristic velocity V (k1 ∝ m*^(1/5) V^(2/5)), so V acts as a stiffness input in quasi-static compaction; the SE modulus 1.35 GPa entering E* is a calibrated input. The global damping term −γv_i in ① takes a large share of the plate reaction during compression (ledger DEMP-01, open) — see the Problem 4 slide. Particle–particle and particle–wall contacts use the same model.

v32_text: Sources: CLAUDE.md "3D MPM compaction — 3-fix calibration" (K = E/(3(1−2ν)) = 25.5 GPa vs DFT B0 26.23); our DFT E_VRH 22.06 GPa; Bazzoun 2026 [8] uses E_SE = 22.1 GPa for Li6PS5Cl; the sulfide-glass value 24 GPa (75Li2S·25P2S5, Sakuda 2013 [3]) is a different material system and is not used on the slide. σy = 0.30 GPa was selected in the pure-SE calibration sweep (0.15 → 5.6 %, 0.20 → 6.7 %, 0.25 → 9.0 %, 0.30 → 10.0 %). Claims ledger CL-94: the pure-SE 10 % value is a calibration target (lab standard sample, unpublished); it is not a literature anchor — our earlier literature attribution was withdrawn. Shear-only softening (ν = 0.49) keeps K = 25.5 GPa close to the DFT reference B0 = 26.23 GPa; softening the bulk modulus over-crushed the bed. "Tested alternatives" = DPC volumetric cap and real-E runs (docs/mpm_dpc_cap_crosscheck.md); the statement is limited to the tested models. Scaffold calculations (AM skeleton from the DEM bed) — status: Earlier: cell-filled SE, bidirectional servo — historical, not a DEM-seeded validation. Current registered runs: DEM-seeded SE, stress-controlled servo — f = 0 completed; f(a) execution failed. AM-load-sharing hypothesis: verdict pending. The current statuses refer to the registered servo runs (--protocol servo; primary endpoint = final thickness after servo convergence). AM load sharing remains a candidate explanation for over-compaction; the final hypothesis verdict is pending. The earlier thickness agreement is not shown: it comes from a different initialization and loading protocol and cannot serve as the validation value of the DEM-seeded runs (SEM-02). Literature crop: So et al., J. Electrochem. Soc. 168, 030538 (2021) [9], Fig. 4a — relative density vs pressure of a sulfide SE with their contact-plasticity parameter (experimental points from Sakuda et al.): a literature example of calibrating an effective contact parameter on pure-SE compaction data. Planned lab anchor (replaces the earlier "validation pending" row; no results yet): docs/session_20260923_progress.md 10-14 entries — EIS plan: LPSCl pellet 0.1 g (10 mm diameter, 300 MPa) as the σ₀ reference; NCM polycrystalline and single-crystal pellets of 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 g (six pellets, EIS + DC polarization); composite and Li-In electron-blocking cells after the NCM pellets; the small-particle SE pellet also gives a geometric porosity (true density unverified) as the pure-SE compaction check; a large-particle LPSCl pellet tests the particle-size factor (listed by the author on 10-14 for this deck; the progress log of 10-14 evening still records it as a recommendation awaiting an answer).

v32_text: Sources: docs/reviews/findings.json DEMP-01 (open: global viscous damping 0.5 during stabilization and compression, 1e-5 during relaxation; the stop criterion |F_plate|/A ≥ 0.30 deck MPa includes the damping drag; one 7:3 bed: drag −γΣv_z = 434.3 N = 57.9 % of the 750 N target (deck units: 0.30 deck MPa × plate area 0.0025 in deck units; docs/dem_governing_equations_background_20261011.md §9); after the plate stops the network pressure relaxes to 165 MPa), MV-01, MV-02 and MV-08 (open); docs/data/ps73_damping_branch_20261007/README.md §1 (original run, relaxation end at fixed platen 165.34 MPa), §4 (predictions B1 and B2 registered before the run), §12-4 (branch B on ibb, job 271368: stop step 3,125,000, 111.052 µm, ε_sphere 14.953 %, 300.906 MPa, drag 434.18 N = 57.89 %; servo hold at 750 N with damping 1e-5 to step 3,735,000, 122 chunks, CONVERGED flag, 105.842 µm, ε_sphere 10.769 %, 299.274 MPa; atoms 160,420 → 160,407, 13 SE lost, AM unchanged; plane-load NCM–NCM share 52.1 → 58.1 %, judgement on hold). B1 equals the registered stop state; B2 (104.9 µm, band 103–107 µm; ε_sphere 10.0 %, band 8.3–11.7 %) contains the result. Figure F_p4 is redrawn from these recorded values only (docs/seminar_20261013/figs_v3/make_seminar_figs_v32.py). Qualifiers: one bed, one composition, one checkpoint; model-internal diagnostic values. (i) The CONVERGED flag does not certify static equilibrium (MV-01). (ii) The servo deck re-creates the plate and wall fixes, which also resets the normal plastic contact history, so B is a combined protocol (history reset + damping drop + force hold); the registered follow-up protocol includes a reset of the plate contact history (MV-02). (iii) The atom-count guard does not certify conservation; the 13 lost particles are SE (MV-08). Wording (docs/reviews/codex_review_model_validation_20261008.md Q11): relative to the existing dynamic stop state, the registered follow-up protocol changed thickness and sphere-volume porosity by −5.210 µm and −4.184 %p; only after separate equilibrium and conservation checks pass may the end point be read as the nominal static 300 MPa state; the comparison is limited to this bed and loading history. ε_sphere is the sphere-volume porosity (overlap counted twice), a different convention from the exact-union porosity shown earlier. The porosity and load-sharing slides use the original protocol (generation 1).
v33_text: Sources: docs/reviews/findings.json DEMP-01 (open: global viscous damping 0.5 during stabilization and compression, 1e-5 during relaxation; the stop criterion |F_plate|/A ≥ 0.30 deck MPa includes the damping drag; one 7:3 bed: drag −γΣv_z = 434.3 N = 57.9 % of the 750 N target (deck units: 0.30 deck MPa × plate area 0.0025 in deck units; docs/dem_governing_equations_background_20261011.md §9); after the plate stops the network pressure relaxes to 165 MPa), MV-01, MV-02 and MV-08 (open); docs/data/ps73_damping_branch_20261007/README.md §1 (original run, relaxation end at fixed platen 165.34 MPa), §4 (predictions B1 and B2 registered before the run), §12-4 (branch B on ibb, job 271368: stop step 3,125,000, 111.052 µm, ε_sphere 14.953 %, 300.906 MPa, drag 434.18 N = 57.89 %; servo hold at 750 N with damping 1e-5 to step 3,735,000, 122 chunks, CONVERGED flag, 105.842 µm, ε_sphere 10.769 %, 299.274 MPa; atoms 160,420 → 160,407, 13 SE lost, AM unchanged; plane-load NCM–NCM share 52.1 → 58.1 %, judgement on hold). B1 equals the registered stop state; B2 (104.9 µm, band 103–107 µm; ε_sphere 10.0 %, band 8.3–11.7 %) contains the result; the shaded band in (b) is this registered prediction band — a model prediction registered before the run, not an experimental range or a statistical confidence interval. Figure F_p4_v33 is redrawn from these recorded values only (docs/seminar_20261013/figs_v3/make_seminar_figs_v33.py: the drawing code of make_seminar_figs_v32.py with the band label added). Qualifiers: one bed, one composition, one checkpoint; model-internal diagnostic values. (i) The CONVERGED flag does not certify static equilibrium (MV-01). (ii) The servo deck re-creates the plate and wall fixes, which also resets the normal plastic contact history, so B is a combined protocol (history reset + damping drop + force hold); the registered follow-up protocol includes a reset of the plate contact history (MV-02). (iii) The atom-count guard does not certify conservation; the 13 lost particles are SE (MV-08). Wording (docs/reviews/codex_review_model_validation_20261008.md Q11): relative to the existing dynamic stop state, the registered follow-up protocol changed thickness and sphere-volume porosity by −5.210 µm and −4.184 %p; only after separate equilibrium and conservation checks pass may the end point be read as the nominal static 300 MPa state; the comparison is limited to this bed and loading history. M of the NCM-pair Bo 1152 setting is −0.968 / −1.407 / −2.283 (outside the Lacey range [0, 1]); start-state variances differ between settings, so ΔM mixes a start-state difference with the post-rotation difference. Grid sensitivity: no new grid campaign is promised here. Unloading: the contact-history test on ibb passed (H0–H5 all PASS; docs/reviews/dem_unloading_history_test_20261014/README.md); the Codex re-review of the unloading kit returned HOLD (12 findings ULKR-01 … ULKR-12; docs/reviews/codex_review_dem_unloading_kit_20261014.md); the fix plan docs/reviews/dem_unloading_kit_fix_plan_20261014.md was ratified on 10-14 (Q1–Q9 as recommended; docs/session_20260923_progress.md, 10-14 afternoon 2 entry); the main unloading run waits for the Codex re-check. DEM protocol generation 2 — plan only, no runs and no results (docs/session_20260923_progress.md, 10-14 evening entries): stages insertion → stabilization → compression → servo (holding the target force) → relaxation → platen removal → unloading, so the unloading logic is a prerequisite; SE true density 1.64 g/cm³ to match the lab value (true density unverified; canonical cards give 1.64 or 1.86–1.87); E_SE re-calibrated so that a pure-SE bed after 300 MPa and relaxation has a union porosity of 10–13 % (lab standard; the small-particle SE pellet geometric porosity is the check), with ε_sphere still recorded internally — choosing ε_union alone cannot resolve a mismatch with a mass-based porosity (docs/reviews/codex_review_model_validation_20261008.md MV-03); Heckel analysis redone, because a slope against the nominal stop pressure is an apparent coefficient of the old protocol (same review, Q2). Design points: compression damping, a static stop rule, no plate re-creation at the servo switch, conservation checks; generation-1 beds stay as labelled results. Next: plan document with canonical literature cards → author ratification → Codex.

Equations ①–⑤, the force diagram and the process strip are copied from the author's 10-09 slide: equation objects and pictures unchanged, Korean labels translated, project header removed. Qualifiers: these are representative equations based on the LIGGGHTS-PUBLIC 3.8.0 hooke/hysteresis model [2], read from the source code, not re-derived by a run; equation ② uses the small-overlap approximation ℓᵢⱼ ≈ Rᵢnᵢⱼ — on the spherical-particle path the implemented lever arm has magnitude Rᵢ − δᵢⱼ/2 (contact radius cri = radi − 0.5·deltan; LIGGGHTS-PUBLIC commit 3d5c00f, surface_model_default.h lines 173–188 and tangential_model_history.h lines 254–261; docs/dem_governing_equations_background_20261011.md §3.1); the linear hysteretic law (loading stiffness k1, unloading/reloading stiffness k2, adhesion branch −k_c δ) follows Luding 2008 [1]; ③ shows the non-saturated branch only (the saturated branch and the k2(δmax) interpolation are in the report); ④ shows the spring part (tangential damping in non-slip steps is omitted); k_t = k_n in this model; the rolling torque uses k_n δ, not the hysteretic normal force; the CDT rolling torque is zero when the relative angular velocity is zero (the direction ω_r/‖ω_r‖ is used only for ‖ω_r‖ > 0; rolling_model_cdt.h lines 94 and 138; torsion torque off); k1 depends on mass and the characteristic velocity V (k1 ∝ m*^(1/5) V^(2/5)), so V acts as a stiffness input in quasi-static compaction; the SE modulus 1.35 GPa entering E* is a calibrated input. The global damping term −γv_i in ① takes a large share of the plate reaction during compression (ledger DEMP-01, open) — see the Problem 4 slide. Particle–particle and particle–wall contacts use the same model.

text: Fixed-shape DEM limits and the material point method (MPM)
Our fixed-shape implementation has no shape change and no yield cap:
overlap is the only plasticity proxy
; the softened SE modulus (1.35 vs ≈ 22 GPa) is an
J2 plasticity on a background grid:
that a fixed-shape sphere cannot represent; active material is kept rigid (DEM skeleton), only the electrolyte flows.

text: Sources: docs/dem_governing_equations_background_20261011.md (§5.3; §10.3 literature counts; §11 limits); CLAUDE.md MPM sections (2026-06-07 … 06-17). In one 7:3 bed, global viscous damping carries 58 % of the plate reaction during compression — an open issue (damping share 57.9 % measured on one 7:3 bed during compression; ledger DEMP-01, open). Selected literature survey (22 studies; author classification, not a systematic review): softened SE modulus 0/22; yield or hardness cap 7/22; linear hysteretic law 1/22; global damping in dry compaction none. Young's modulus reference: our DFT E_VRH = 22.06 GPa (literature DEM input 22.1 GPa, Bazzoun 2026 [8]); the bulk modulus K / B0 = 26.23 GPa is a separate quantity; the glass-electrolyte value 24 GPa (Sakuda 2013 [3]) is a different material system. The DEM statement is about this implementation (fixed spherical shapes, hooke/hysteresis), not about DEM in general. MPM parameters: 2D E = 1.53 GPa, σy = 0.15 GPa; 3D E = 1.53 GPa, ν = 0.49, σy = 0.30 GPa (next slide). Presenter figure (right, blank): MPM 3D render of the DEM-scaffold bed (AM fixed, SE material points), e.g. python3 scripts/viz_mpm_morphology.py --se <SE material points .npy> --scaffold <AM scaffold .csv> --y 0.5 --out morphology.png (actual files required; MPM renders are not tracked in the repository). Do not present the MPM image as an independent validation of the DEM bed.

text: Sources: CLAUDE.md "3D MPM compaction — 3-fix calibration" (K = E/(3(1−2ν)) = 25.5 GPa vs DFT B0 26.23); our DFT E_VRH 22.06 GPa; Bazzoun 2026 [8] uses E_SE = 22.1 GPa for Li6PS5Cl; the sulfide-glass value 24 GPa (75Li2S·25P2S5, Sakuda 2013 [3]) is a different material system and is not used on the slide. σy = 0.30 GPa was selected in the pure-SE calibration sweep (0.15 → 5.6 %, 0.20 → 6.7 %, 0.25 → 9.0 %, 0.30 → 10.0 %). Claims ledger CL-94: the pure-SE 10 % value is a calibration target (lab standard sample, unpublished); it is not a literature anchor — our earlier literature attribution was withdrawn. Shear-only softening (ν = 0.49) keeps K = 25.5 GPa close to the DFT reference B0 = 26.23 GPa; softening the bulk modulus over-crushed the bed. "Tested alternatives" = DPC volumetric cap and real-E runs (docs/mpm_dpc_cap_crosscheck.md); the statement is limited to the tested models. Scaffold calculations (AM skeleton from the DEM bed) — status: Earlier: cell-filled SE, bidirectional servo — historical, not a DEM-seeded validation. Current registered runs: DEM-seeded SE, stress-controlled servo — f = 0 completed; f(a) execution failed. AM-load-sharing hypothesis: verdict pending. The current statuses refer to the registered servo runs (--protocol servo; primary endpoint = final thickness after servo convergence). AM load sharing remains a candidate explanation for over-compaction; the final hypothesis verdict is pending. The earlier thickness agreement is not shown: it comes from a different initialization and loading protocol and cannot serve as the validation value of the DEM-seeded runs (SEM-02). Soc. 168, 030538 (2021) [9], Fig. 4a — relative density vs pressure of a sulfide SE with their contact-plasticity parameter (experimental points from Sakuda et al.): a literature example of calibrating an effective contact parameter on pure-SE compaction data. text: Sources: CLAUDE.md "σ 를 내는 솔버는 둘이다" table and CL-81. Finite-volume conservation on the phase grid gives electrical (σ, φ) and thermal (κ, T) transport on the same structure. The voxel solver has no interface-resistance term by default (the film mechanism exists but is off): this makes it an ideal-interface model and an upper bound only for the same geometry, phase properties and boundary conditions — not a physical upper bound; geometric necks still cost resistance inside the voxel grid. The 4.04× (contact-free / full network, n = 157) is a ratio inside the contact-network model. Additives: carbon fibres (VGCF) as diameter-preserving segments, PTFE as a centre-line insulator, a conductive polymer as true-diameter spheres. Pre-registered 104-arm study: the electronic-conductivity order across 1–4 wt% VGCF holds across the tested voxel sizes and grid-origin offsets (72/72) — docs/data/phase_a_rep100_20260930/README.md (104 arms, 72/72 adjacent-composition comparisons with no threshold violation; order only is the registered estimand; increments are technical report only; replay difference 0.00000 %); docs/report_20261021 G6 (voxel σe means; contact resistance not included; figure F_vgcf redrawn from G6). The numerical rule maps this contrast to the registered "no segregation" category. This does not establish compliance with the original registration, equivalence, or a physical absence of segregation (this model, this drum, the tested inputs and this bin convention). Coarser grids (report only): 12×12×3 Δ −0.0156, SE 0.0058 (ambiguous); 8×8×2 Δ +0.0081, SE 0.0144. Negative control (no cohesion): M ≥ 0.8 in all three grids; floor check 10/10; flatness 30/30; QC 30/30. The two cohesion matrices differ in NCM–NCM and NCM–wall adhesion together; the comparison is not a reproduction of real coating or of powder flowability. Contract qualifier (Codex wording, 2026-09-28): the result is a comparison of mixing indices after eight revolutions in the specified soft-contact model; in the reference state the maximum stored-frame overlap was 4.7–5.8 % particle–particle and 4.5–5.7 % at the wall, so the registered 1 % condition was not met; the effect of the overlap error on the mixing index has not been verified. Presenter figure (right, blank): bed view of one run, layered start and after eight revolutions (webapp bed view; display only). Literature on the index (context): Lacey's M is normalized to a random-mixture variance; Hersey 1975 [4] noted that homogeneity measures referenced to a random mixture are not satisfactory for ordered mixtures. Mixing in which small particles adhere to carrier-particle surfaces was called ordered mixing by Hersey 1975 [4]; Egermann & Orr 1983 [5] proposed calling this type interactive mixing and reserved "ordered" for homogeneity beyond random (σ < σ_R) (wording of docs/hetero_thesis.md §2-5). The M values here use the random reference.

text: Sources: docs/hetero_thesis.md (ratified 2026-10-05) §2-1 · §2-2 · §2-8. With W_AA = 2γ_A, W_SS = 2γ_S and an assumed geometric-mean rule W_AS = 2√(γ_A γ_S), ΔW = W_AA + W_SS − 2 W_AS = 2(√γ_A − √γ_S)² ≥ 0 (J m⁻²) is a per-area comparison at equal contact areas (ΔU = −A·ΔW for a common area A); real exchanges also change contact areas, deformation energy and dynamics, so contact counts alone do not fix the sign of the released energy. Pull-off force (JKR) scales with W·R*: at equal W the weight-normalized SE–SE adhesion is about 194× that of the large-NCM self-pair (arithmetic estimate), but for one SE particle the SE–NCM pull-off exceeds SE–SE by 2r_NCM/(r_NCM + r_SE) = 1.8 (large NCM) and 1.6 (small NCM). Under the geometric-mean rule the SE–SE pull-off exceeds the SE–large-NCM pull-off only if γ_NCM/γ_SE < 0.309 (small NCM: 0.391) — a two-contact force comparison, not a necessary or sufficient condition for cluster survival; that ratio is not known (open decision). Predictions P1–P3 of the thesis: uncoated beds keep SE–SE clustering above random; coating removes it; the mixing difference carries into the compacted SE pathway. The all-pair CED runs also scale SE–SE cohesion; the model is not calibrated to measured surface energies or coating selectivity, so the CED-scaling runs do not validate a surface-energy-based coating mechanism. Left figure: docs/data/mixer_highbo_devu_prelim_20261006/devu_contact.json — fraction of SE in SE–SE clusters (second revolution, 100 frames): 0.400 [0.143, 0.542] low NCM–NCM cohesion; 0.954 [0.875, 0.957] all-pair CED ×10; 0.988 [0.981, 0.988] all-pair CED ×14.42 (ranges = dump-resolution [certain, possible], not confidence intervals; one seed; development data; the lower bounds of the two higher settings exceed the comparator upper bound). Confirmatory 18-run block: registered, on hold after the Codex rounds (docs/reviews/mixer_highbo_prereg_20260927.md). Literature (canonical cards): Mixing in which small particles adhere to carrier-particle surfaces was called ordered mixing by Hersey 1975 [4]; Egermann & Orr 1983 [5] proposed calling this type interactive mixing and reserved "ordered" for homogeneity beyond random (σ < σ_R) (wording of docs/hetero_thesis.md §2-5). shapes.name: Rectangle 4
text: Fixed-shape DEM limits and the material point method (MPM)
Our fixed-shape implementation has no shape change and no yield cap:
overlap is the only plasticity proxy
; the softened SE modulus (1.35 vs ≈ 22 GPa) is an
J2 plasticity on a background grid:
that a fixed-shape sphere cannot represent; active material is kept rigid (DEM skeleton), only the electrolyte flows.

text: Sources: docs/dem_governing_equations_background_20261011.md (§5.3; §10.3 literature counts; §11 limits); CLAUDE.md MPM sections (2026-06-07 … 06-17). In one 7:3 bed, global viscous damping carries 58 % of the plate reaction during compression — an open issue (damping share 57.9 % measured on one 7:3 bed during compression; ledger DEMP-01, open). Selected literature survey (22 studies; author classification, not a systematic review): softened SE modulus 0/22; yield or hardness cap 7/22; linear hysteretic law 1/22; global damping in dry compaction none. Young's modulus reference: our DFT E_VRH = 22.06 GPa (literature DEM input 22.1 GPa, Bazzoun 2026 [8]); the bulk modulus K / B0 = 26.23 GPa is a separate quantity; the glass-electrolyte value 24 GPa (Sakuda 2013 [3]) is a different material system. The DEM statement is about this implementation (fixed spherical shapes, hooke/hysteresis), not about DEM in general. MPM parameters: 2D E = 1.53 GPa, σy = 0.15 GPa; 3D E = 1.53 GPa, ν = 0.49, σy = 0.30 GPa (next slide). text: Sources: CLAUDE.md "σ 를 내는 솔버는 둘이다" table and CL-81. Finite-volume conservation on the phase grid gives electrical (σ, φ) and thermal (κ, T) transport on the same structure. The voxel solver has no interface-resistance term by default (the film mechanism exists but is off): this makes it an ideal-interface model and an upper bound only for the same geometry, phase properties and boundary conditions — not a physical upper bound; geometric necks still cost resistance inside the voxel grid. The 4.04× (contact-free / full network, n = 157) is a ratio inside the contact-network model. Additives: carbon fibres (VGCF) as diameter-preserving segments, PTFE as a centre-line insulator, a conductive polymer as true-diameter spheres. Pre-registered 104-arm study: the electronic-conductivity order across 1–4 wt% VGCF holds across the tested voxel sizes and grid-origin offsets (72/72) — docs/data/phase_a_rep100_20260930/README.md (104 arms, 72/72 adjacent-composition comparisons with no threshold violation; order only is the registered estimand; increments are technical report only; replay difference 0.00000 %); docs/report_20261021 G6 (voxel σe means; contact resistance not included; figure F_vgcf redrawn from G6). The plotted means are the original campaign (VGCF E = 10 GPa, docs/data/phase_a_104arms_20260921); the 100 GPa replication (docs/data/phase_a_rep100_20260930) also keeps the order 72/72 with slightly different means, so the plotted values are not the 100 GPa means. Stamp conventions: CLAUDE.md SR-01 (sphere stamp, centerline PTFE = CL-60). Presenter figures (left, blank): (i) contact-network current pathways of the 7:3 bed — scripts/network_current.py dump <7:3 result folder> → webapp DEM 3D viewer "current flow" (same bed, same H0/FULL ionic solution, 1 V, colour = j = |I|/A; "top 50 % of current" = edges carrying the top half of the current share, not the top half by count); (ii) STEP3 phase grid and the 1 V current-density field of the same voxel solution (A cm⁻²; state origin, voxel size, phase mapping, electrode rule, run hash).

text: Sources: docs/hetero_thesis.md (ratified 2026-10-05) §2-1 · §2-2 · §2-8. With W_AA = 2γ_A, W_SS = 2γ_S and an assumed geometric-mean rule W_AS = 2√(γ_A γ_S), ΔW = W_AA + W_SS − 2 W_AS = 2(√γ_A − √γ_S)² ≥ 0 (J m⁻²) is a per-area comparison at equal contact areas (ΔU = −A·ΔW for a common area A); real exchanges also change contact areas, deformation energy and dynamics, so contact counts alone do not fix the sign of the released energy. Pull-off force (JKR) scales with W·R*: at equal W the weight-normalized SE–SE adhesion is about 194× that of the large-NCM self-pair (arithmetic estimate), but for one SE particle the SE–NCM pull-off exceeds SE–SE by 2r_NCM/(r_NCM + r_SE) = 1.8 (large NCM) and 1.6 (small NCM). Under the geometric-mean rule the SE–SE pull-off exceeds the SE–large-NCM pull-off only if γ_NCM/γ_SE < 0.309 (small NCM: 0.391) — a two-contact force comparison, not a necessary or sufficient condition for cluster survival; that ratio is not known (open decision). Predictions P1–P3 of the thesis: uncoated beds keep SE–SE clustering above random; coating removes it; the mixing difference carries into the compacted SE pathway. The all-pair CED runs also scale SE–SE cohesion; the model is not calibrated to measured surface energies or coating selectivity, so the CED-scaling runs do not validate a surface-energy-based coating mechanism. Left figure: docs/data/mixer_highbo_devu_prelim_20261006/devu_contact.json — fraction of SE in SE–SE clusters (second revolution, 100 frames): 0.400 [0.143, 0.542] low NCM–NCM cohesion; 0.954 [0.875, 0.957] all-pair CED ×10; 0.988 [0.981, 0.988] all-pair CED ×14.42 (ranges = dump-resolution [certain, possible], not confidence intervals; one seed; development data; the lower bounds of the two higher settings exceed the comparator upper bound). Confirmatory 18-run block: registered, on hold after the Codex rounds (docs/reviews/mixer_highbo_prereg_20260927.md). Literature (canonical cards): Mixing in which small particles adhere to carrier-particle surfaces was called ordered mixing by Hersey 1975 [4]; Egermann & Orr 1983 [5] proposed calling this type interactive mixing and reserved "ordered" for homogeneity beyond random (σ < σ_R) (wording of docs/hetero_thesis.md §2-5). NCM side of the surface-energy ratio: Kim 2012 [7] — clean-slab DFT (GGA+U, 0 K) surface energies of the end members LiNiO₂ and LiCoO₂ (not NCM) are lower for LiNiO₂ on all computed facets; these are bond-breaking energies of clean slabs, not the dispersion adhesion W of particle contacts, so the uncoated NCM / SE ratio stays open (docs/hetero_thesis.md §2-8).
